# The bound of a dot product of two limbs, as a function of the number of terms

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `bound_dot_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Numbers of `T` that bound expressions of $m$ from above, valid when the mask $\mathit{ok}$ is true:

$$g \ge \frac{m \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_2\_2})}{1 - m \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_2\_2})}, \qquad t \ge m \mathrm{tiny}(\mathtt{mul\_2\_2}) (1 + g).$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `traits<Expansion<T, 2>>::dot(n)` | `std::size_t` | `Bound<T>` | $m = n$, a count of `T` rounded up; `unit` is $g$, `tiny` is $t$ |

`T` is `float` or `double`; `kairn::traits<T>` is also `kairn::traits<float>`, `kairn::traits<double>` and `kairn::traits<Expansion<T, 1>>`; header `kairn/kairn.hpp` (`traits.hpp`). `constexpr`, with the same bits at compile time and at run time; where the mask is false the result's `unit` and `tiny` are $+\infty$, which claims nothing, and in a constant expression the call does not compile ([Functions on arrays](batch.md#the-bound-as-a-function-of-the-length)).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $m = 0$ or $m \ge 1$, as a number of terms is.
- The format contains $\tfrac12$: $\eta \le \tfrac12$, as `float` and `double` do.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- when $\mathit{ok}$ is true, $m \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_2\_2}) \le \frac{1}{2}$.
- when $\mathit{ok}$ is true, $g \ge \frac{m \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_2\_2})}{1 - m \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_2\_2})}$.
- when $\mathit{ok}$ is true, $t \ge m \mathrm{tiny}(\mathtt{mul\_2\_2}) (1 + g)$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 4 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `bound_dot_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/BoundKernels.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/BoundKernels.v), against `bound_dot_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions bound_dot_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition bound_dot_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (4 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall m : R,
  fmt emin prec m ->
  (m = 0 \/ 1 <= m) ->
  eta emin <= / 2 ->
  let '(g, t, ok) := bound_dot_2 emin prec tie_even m in
  fmt emin prec g /\
  fmt emin prec t /\
  (ok = true -> (m * (4 * u prec ^ 2)) <= (1 / 2)) /\
  (ok = true -> ((m * (4 * u prec ^ 2)) / (1 - (m * (4 * u prec ^ 2)))) <= g) /\
  (ok = true -> ((m * ((3 / 2) * eta emin)) * (1 + g)) <= t).
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `bound_dot_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the exported bound of a dot product as a function of n (milestone2.md). **License:** proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/bound_dot_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/bound_dot_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The exported bound of a dot product of m terms of 2-limb numbers (milestone2.md, "The bound as a
# function of n"). When the mask ok is true,
#   |computed - sum x_i y_i| <= g sum |x_i y_i| + t
# with g >= gamma_m(eps), eps the larger of the proved units of mul_2_2 and add_2_2 (that of
# mul_2_2, 4 u^2, from precision 4), and t >= m tiny (1 + g), tiny the absolute term of mul_2_2.
# ok also asks for g <= 1, which the step from g to 1 + g needs; in binary32 and binary64 the
# first test implies it.
#   tm >= (1 + u) (m tiny + eta / 2)    (for m >= 1; the constant holds the smallest normal number,
#                                        eta / (2u), so that it is not subnormal, as H of the Ball
#                                        cores: milestone2.md asks of no listing a subnormal constant)
#   t  >= m tiny (1 + g)

a  = prod(m, const up((1+u)*(unit(mul_2_2)+eta/2)))
aa = prod(m, const up((1+u)^2*(unit(mul_2_2)+eta)))
# d = 2a, as milestone2.md writes it: a product by 2, exact, and not add(a, a), which GCC turns
# into a * 2 and contracts into the next addition (rule R1 refuses it).
d  = prod(a, const up(2))
w  = add(d, const up(1+2*u))
g  = prod(aa, w)
tm = prod(m, const up((1+u)^2*(tiny(mul_2_2)+eta)+eta/(2*u)))
wg = add(g, const up(1+2*u))
t  = prod(tm, wg)
oa = le(a, const up(1/4))
ob = le(g, const up(1))
ok = and(oa, ob)
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 2**: the runs of commit `5f597fb` and the supplementary run of commit `8ee5ed9`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#bound_dot_2)).

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
